_readme: Query expansion. When any string in 'terms' appears in a visitor's question,
the words in 'expandsTo' are added to the search before ranking runs. The
visitor never sees this; it only widens what the ranker can find.
THE RULE FOR ADDING ENTRIES — this one was learned the hard way.
Only map a word the visitor uses to a DIFFERENT word the site uses: an
acronym to its full name, or a synonym to the site's own term. Never 'enrich'
a term that already matches the site's vocabulary, and never add generic
words.
Two examples of what goes wrong. Expanding 'padlet' to 'Padlet collaboration
tool' added the words 'collaboration' and 'tool', which then let pages about
collaborative growth and Moodle tools outscore the actual Padlet page.
Expanding 'peer review' to 'peer observation teaching' added 'teaching',
which appears in dozens of URL paths and made a conference session stub look
like a confident answer. Both expansions made search worse than none.
Entries marked "confirm": true are sector-standard expansions that CADI has
not verified. Check them before relying on them.
Deliberately absent: SELL and gprof, because nobody has been able to say what
they stand for. Ask CADI, then add them. Also absent: APEX, PrepUP, Docebo,
Turnitin and SharePoint — external systems with no CADI page. Those belong in
external-links.json once CADI confirms the destinations.
